final.summary: Recommended: fused. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.91 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.08 °C, 73% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **We're right at the heat limit.** On the hottest stretch, the crew's body temperature is expected to get very close to the safe maximum, with almost no room to spare. Watch for signs of heat stress, enforce water and shade breaks, and pull anyone who looks off.

**Storms cut the day short, so not everything gets done.** No outdoor work from 1 to 3 PM because of lightning and severe thunderstorms. Even so, about three-quarters of the most important work gets finished. Expect some tasks to carry over.

**Kofi stays off the hardest jobs in the heat.** He's new and his body isn't used to these conditions yet. We looked at two other plans. One has Kofi do the cable pulling in the cool early hours, but it gets slightly less done with the same heat risk. The other squeezes out a little more work, but it pushes the crew even closer to the heat limit. This plan is the best balance.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
